sec.stack.s: Every name here appears in one of the projects below or in this site's own build.
sec.process.s: Five steps. The first one is free: if the job isn't worth doing, you'll hear it there.
step.audit.d: I look at what's already there, measure speed and weight, and say honestly whether the job is worth doing. Free.
step.arch.d: Data model, content sources, URL structure. Settled before the first line of markup.
step.build.d: Pages are generated from content, and a demo on a real address appears as the work goes.
step.ship.d: Content, figures, headings, and images are checked on every deploy. A wrong number never reaches a visitor.
step.hand.d: The repository moves to you. No subscription, no hostage hosting, no access you don't have.
about.p: I build the whole thing: architecture, backend, frontend, infrastructure and the tests that hold it together. I work online, with clients across time zones. The code of every project is public — you can read it before you pay for it.
footer.note: Built without frameworks or third-party libraries.
sec.journal.s: New case studies, write-ups of the techniques behind them, and short updates. The dates show the work is still going, not finished a year ago.

sec.faq.s: The terms people ask about in their first message. Answered here so they don't have to be answered by email.
faq.time.q: How long does the work take?
faq.time.a1: In working days, counted from the moment the deposit and the materials arrive. A one-page site takes 4–6 days, a landing page with a quiz 6–9, a site with a price list and sections 10–15, a move off Tilda or Wix 14–21. A simple bot takes 2–4 days, a booking bot with a database and an admin panel 5–10, a channel on autopilot 7–12, a utility bot with subscriptions 7–12, a lead parser 7–14. An integration with a CRM or with payments adds 2–5 days.
faq.time.a2: What holds the schedule is not the build but how ready the materials are: copy, price list, photos, access. Second comes the speed of approvals: if the final call is made by someone other than the person I'm writing to, the schedule doubles. Third is scope. The build itself matters least.
faq.scope.q: What is included, and what is a separate stage?
faq.scope.a1: Everything technical is included: mobile layout, schema.org markup, speed, analytics, deployment, and a machine-readable summary for AI search engines.
faq.scope.a2: Separate stages: keyword research and the copy written for it, Google Business Profile and maps, copywriting itself. Design defaults to my own base fitted to your brand: your colours, fonts and photos. A bespoke design with concepts is discussed separately, and with finished mockups the schedule is shorter.
faq.pay.a1: 50% up front, 50% on handover. Projects above ₽60,000 are split into three payments of 40/30/30 against checkpoints; monthly support is paid a month ahead. I don't start without a deposit.
faq.pay.a2: Card or SBP; in Thailand and Vietnam a normal local transfer in baht or dong — I hold accounts in both countries; outside the region Wise, Payoneer, or USDT. On freelance platforms I work through escrow only. Two rounds of revisions are included, anything beyond that is hourly — written into the brief in advance.
faq.code.a1: You do. The repository moves to your account whole, not as an archive — after the final payment. Until then the project runs on my server: you can look at it, test it and show it to anyone. If seeing the code from day one matters, I'll open read access straight away and transfer ownership on payment.
faq.code.a2: Everything the code needs to run goes with it: deployment configuration, tests and automated checks, an administrator's guide. Keys and passwords are handed over separately — they are not in the repository.
faq.monthly.a1: For a site, none. There is one cost: the domain, around ₽1,000–2,000 a year, registered in your name. Hosting is free, and you edit prices and copy yourself — no developer needed for that. If you'd rather not bother, support costs ₽3,000–8,000 a month, but that's an option, not a condition.
faq.monthly.a2: A bot is different: it lives on a server, from $5 a month, billed to you directly; a bot with AI adds model access, also on your account. You can watch it yourself or hand that to me: ₽5,000–15,000 a month, ₽10,000–25,000 for a channel on autopilot. The first month is free either way. Every account — domain, server, analytics — is registered in your name, so nothing ties you to me.
faq.legacy.q: Will you take on someone else's project?
faq.legacy.a1: Yes, by the hour: ₽2,500–4,000 an hour, three hours minimum. I start with 2–4 hours to look through it — I read the code and tell you what's there and how long it will take. I won't quote a fixed price for code I haven't opened: that would be unfair to both of us.
faq.legacy.a2: If it turns out that rewriting is cheaper than fixing, you get both numbers: fixing as it stands costs this much, but the frame stays fragile and the next change will be expensive again; rewriting costs more now and less to maintain. You decide. I won't quietly rewrite it and call it a fix.
faq.legacy.a3: I won't take it on without access to the code and the server, on a "fix it but don't touch anything" basis, or on a stack I don't work with.
faq.start.q: What do you need from me to start?
faq.start.a1: Four things: answers to the brief, your sign-off on a short scope document, the deposit, and one person who makes the final calls.
faq.start.a2: Access. For a bot — the BotFather token, access to the CRM, spreadsheets or payment provider with their documentation, the IDs of admins and chats. For a site — the domain or permission to register it, access to the current site and hosting if it's a move, an analytics account.
faq.start.a3: Materials. Copy about your services; the full price list in a single file, every item; your own photos, not stock; the logo in vector; contacts and the messenger where enquiries should land. For a channel on autopilot — a list of sources and 5–10 sample posts in your voice.
faq.start.a4: The price list has to be complete and in one file for a reason: prices live in a single source, so a number is changed once and changes everywhere — in the table, in the service descriptions and in the markup search engines read. And one organisational thing: answers within one working day. Disappear for a week and the schedule moves by a week.
